claims.text: High-entropy alloys comprise five or more metallic elements in equal or near-equal atomic ratios and can form simple solid-solution phases.
The initial nanoparticles are homogeneous solid solutions.
Structural and chemical stability is governed by a balance between configurational entropy and lattice-distortion-induced kinetic stabilization.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the random solid-solution phase against intermetallic formation or phase segregation.
Atomic-size differences among constituent elements produce severe lattice distortion in high-entropy alloys.
Severe lattice distortion lowers atomic diffusivity.
Reduced atomic diffusivity provides a kinetic barrier against phase separation and chemical ordering.
High-density overlapping energy barriers associated with chemical or lattice disorder stabilize the nanoparticles against phase separation.
Atomic-size mismatches within approximately 15% are sufficient for the proposed lattice-distortion stabilization.
Lattice distortion elevates an effective temperature that kinetically hinders phase separation and surface segregation.
Under inert and reducing atmospheres, heated nanoparticles will retain a largely homogeneous solid solution with minimal phase separation or compositional inhomogeneity.
Oxidizing atmospheres create surface chemical driving forces or chemical-potential gradients that can overcome the kinetic barrier locally.
Oxidizing conditions will cause limited surface segregation or rearrangement while leaving the nanoparticle core stable.
The core under oxidizing conditions remains thermodynamically stabilized by the kinetic barrier from lattice distortion.
The proposed stability behavior applies across 473–1923 K.
Greater atomic-size mismatch or very strong oxidizing conditions may cause deviations from the predicted stability.
The relative stability can be tested by heating matched nanoparticles under inert, reducing, and oxidizing atmospheres and monitoring phase, composition, and strain in situ.

contradictions.description: The mechanism identifies lattice distortion as a kinetic barrier, but the predicted outcome calls the core 'thermodynamically stabilized by the kinetic barrier.' A kinetic impediment can delay equilibration but is not itself thermodynamic stabilization.
